entities.summary: Mani was an Iranian prophet who founded Manichaeism, a religion that flourished in late antiquity, particularly in the Persian Empire (modern-day Iran) and Central Asia. Born in the 3rd century AD, Mani's teachings drew upon Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Buddhism, aiming to reconcile the contradictions of these faiths. His message of a dualistic universe, where good and evil are inextricably linked, resonated with many people, especially in the wake of the Roman Empire's collapse. Mani's influence extended beyond the Iranian Empire, with his followers spreading to the Roman Empire, the Sasanian Empire, and eventually to China. Despite facing persecution and skepticism from early Christian leaders, Mani's legacy endured, with remnants of his teachings found in the works of early Christian writers like Origen. His emphasis on the importance of the material world and the struggle between good and evil also influenced the development of Gnosticism. Mani's life and teachings continue to captivate historians and scholars, offering a unique window into the spiritual and cultural landscape of the ancient world.
